title: CATL Shares Hit All-Time High of 460 Yuan (+5.5%) as China's Scheduled Battery Production Hits Record 249 GWh in May — Third Consecutive Monthly Record
detail: CATL's Shenzhen A-share stock surged 5.50% on May 6, 2026 to close at a new all-time high of 460 yuan per share, driven by data showing China's total scheduled lithium battery production reached 249 GWh in May — a 6% month-on-month increase and the third consecutive monthly production record for the Chinese battery sector. The broader battery sector rallied in tandem: Gotion High-Tech rose 4.95% and Eve Energy gained 4.06% at the close. The production record reflects surging demand from both the EV sector and the rapidly expanding grid-scale battery energy storage market, where global BESS shipments reached 421.2 GWh in 2025 (+75.5% YoY) with 600 GWh projected for 2026. CATL's dominant position is underscored by fresh Q1 2026 data: the company holds a 40.7% global EV battery market share (January–March 2026), up from its ~39.2% 2025 full-year figure, with Q1 production of 99.5 GWh (+15.2% YoY). CATL's record stock price reflects investor confidence following its $5B Hong Kong share placement (April 30), the 60 GWh HyperStrong sodium-ion deal, and the company's Q1 2026 net profit of ¥20.7 billion (~$2.8B, +49% YoY) — its highest quarterly profit ever.

title: Q1 2026 Global EV Battery Market Grows 9.1% to 244.6 GWh; CATL Commands 40.7%, Korean Makers Face Mixed Results
detail: South Korean market research firm SNE Research, reporting on May 6, 2026, found that global production of battery cells for electric vehicles grew 9.1% year-on-year to 244.6 GWh in Q1 2026. CATL extended its dominance with production up 15.2% to 99.5 GWh, capturing a 40.7% global market share — its highest-ever recorded quarterly figure. BYD held second position with 13.7% share. Among South Korean manufacturers, LG Energy Solution ranked first with +6.6% growth to 23.7 GWh, while SK On declined 10.4% to 9.0 GWh and Samsung SDI fell 27.7% to 5.3 GWh — the latter a sharp drop attributed to customer mix changes as major automakers slow premium NMC cell procurement in response to US IRA credit uncertainty. SNE Research characterised the global battery market as entering a 'structural transition phase,' with demand trends diverging by region: declining in China (market saturation at lower price points) and North America (post-IRA credit expiry EV demand softness), while growing in Europe, other Asian markets, and emerging economies. The structural shift is also visible in chemistry: LFP and sodium-ion cells are gaining share relative to NMC as cost-sensitive segments dominate new deployments. Grid storage applications now account for roughly 30% of total battery cell production globally.
